- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 30-day forecasts often start above true values).
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias after recent spikes in price (e.g., after 70–75 range, model jumps to 75+ and holds).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion after sharp peaks; tends to overreact to recent highs.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the horizon, then catch up or overshoot.
- After a spike (e.g., 76+), model often overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged high, missing subsequent pullback.
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when prices are trending down.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to reflect volatility or sudden reversals in the true price path.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — starts from recent high and doesn’t adjust downward even when true price drops.
